Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ashutosh Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Shashidhar Pandey, learned
Additional Government Advocate for the State-O.P. no.1 as well as Sri Shubham Kumar, learned
counsel appearing for the opposite party no.2 and perused the record.

2. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant praying for
quashing of the proceedings of complaint case no. 3468 of 2022 (Tanu Kumar Vs. Smt. Renu Devi
Jadaun and others) under Section 406 Ipc, P.S. Etmaddaula, District Agra, as well as summoning
order dated 02.12.2022 passed by Additional Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 08,

sentences.text: 3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submits that there is matrimonial discord between the parties.
The applicant is the opposite party no.2.

The applicant (wife) had earlier lodged a first information report on 02.12.2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, against the Smt Renu Devi Jadaun vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14450319/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: opposite party no.2
. After investigation charge sheet was filed in the matter.
Thereafter applicant (wife) had filed a case under Section 125 Cr.P.C. for maintenance on 23.11.2020.

Apart from above another FIR was lodged by the applicant on 01.03.2022 against the opposite party no.2, under Sections 323, 504, 506 IPC, in which, it is alleged that the opposite party no.2 along with his other family members stopped the applicant and beaten up her.

He further submits that as a counterblast the opposite party no.2 had filed the instant complaint on 16.03.2022, in which it is alleged that the applicant had walked out with the ornaments of the family.
However, in the statement recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. the opposite party no.2 has not stated anything regarding walking away with no ornaments.

However, in the statement of the witnesses recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C.
there was corroboration regarding allegation of complaint.
4. Counsel for the applicant submits that the entire prosecution is nothing but a counterblast to the proceedings initiated by the applicant against the opposite party no.2.
The instant complaint has been filed only to harass and put undue pressure upon the applicant to compromise the matter.
He further submits that the entire story as narrated in the complaint is bogus.

In fact the story of the complaint is contrary to the statements under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.
5.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for O.P. no.2 have vehemently opposed the application and contended that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant as there is contradictions with the averments of the complaint as well as the statements recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.
6.

From the perusal of material on record, it is evident that the applicant (wife) had earlier filed an FIR under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, thereafter she has filed proceedings under Section 125 Cr.P.C. for maintenance and apart from it, another FIR was lodged by the applicant against the opposite party no.2 and his family members under Sections 323, 504, 506 IPC,
as a counterblast the instant complaint has been filed by the opposite party no.2 only with a view to harass and put undue pressure upon her to compromise the matter.
At this stage only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court.

7. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 has laid down the guidelines under which circumstances the Court should, in its inherent power,
entertain an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The guidelines are as follows:-
"(i) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.
(ii) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.
Smt Renu Devi Jadaun vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14450319/
2

entities.text: Renu Devi Jadaun vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ( iii) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(iv) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(v) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(vi) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the Act concerned (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the Act concerned, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(vii) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fides and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
8. The instant case comes well within the purview of guidelines no. (i), (iii) and (v) of the Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal case (supra), as from the bare reading of the complaint no prima facie case is made out against the applicant and as such the proceedings of the complaint deserves to be set aside and quashed.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the guidelines no. (i), (iii) and (v), framed by the Apex Court in the case of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal case (supra), the application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and the entire proceedings of complaint case no. 3468 of 2022 (Tanu Kumar Vs. Smt. Renu Devi Jadaun and others) under Section 406 IPC, P.S. Etmaddaula, District Agra, as well as summoning order dated 02.12.2022 passed by Additional Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 08, Agra, pending in the court of Additional Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 08, Agra, are quashed.
